chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Safwan from Musa from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Khul' (redemption/divorce by wife's initiative) does not occur until she says: 'I will not obey you in any matter, nor fulfill your oath, nor establish your limit [of authority], so take from me and divorce me.' When she says that, it becomes permissible for him to release her for whatever amount they mutually agree upon, whether little or much. And this does not occur except before a judge (sultan). When she does that, she becomes more in control of herself, without him specifying it as a divorce.

key_terms.الْخُلْعُ: Khul' (divorce initiated by the wife in exchange for financial compensation)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific conditions and legal requirements for Khul' divorce in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the precise verbal formula required for Khul, emphasizing the wife's declaration of inability to observe the husband's rights as the legal trigger for separation. It highlights the procedural necessity of judicial oversight ('at sanad al-sultan') and clarifies that this specific mechanism grants the wife autonomy over her personhood without being classified as a standard revocable divorce, a distinction crucial in Shia fiqh.
